newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: UN says Afghan Taleban willing to ban opium trade.
newsitem.headline: UN says Afghan Taleban willing to ban opium trade.

text.p: Afghanistan's fundamentalist Islamic Taleban have indicated they want to eventually ban opium poppy production, a move that could cut Asia's heroin output by half, United Nations drugs experts said on Tuesday.
Abdul Latif, Asia-Pacific chief of the U.N. International Drug Control Programme, said in an interview that the Taleban oppose poppy cultivation on religious grounds.
But the group, which has imposed strict Islamic rule over the two thirds of Afghanistan it controls, has said it must first find replacement crops for farmers who depend on poppies.

"We have had discussions with them (Taleban) and they are saying that because of their religious belief... they do not favour production of opium, they are against it," Latif, himself an Afghan, said.

"The only reason they have indicated they cannot declare a ban is so many rely on the income, that if the people could be helped to go back to what they were producing before, that they would definitely declare a ban."
Latif said the Taleban were concerned that an immediate ban "would only add to the misery of the people" in the war-battered country.
He said talks with the Taleban, who controlled six poppy growing provinces began two years ago and would continue.
UNDCP director Giovanni Quaglia flew to Taleban headquarters in Kandahar on Sunday to explore how far the Taleban were willing to crack down on the lucrative narcotics trade in their territory.
The Afghan territory under Taleban control includes its richest poppy-growing areas and smuggling routes to Pakistan, Iran and the Central Asian republic of Turkmenistan.
"We would not let any opportunity go by without probing the possibility of doing something to reduce and fight (drug trafficking)," Latif said.
"If that happens, then all of a sudden in Afghanistan itself we would have a major reduction of opium and this is well within the possibility."
Latif estimated Afghanistan produced 2,300 tonnes of opium a year, adding that a ban on poppy cultivation would mean "half of opium production (in Asia) would no longer exist".
The other half of the opium output comes from southeast Asia, mainly the "Golden Triangle" countries of Burma, Thailand and Laos, drugs experts said.
Opium is the raw material from which heroin is derived.

Latif said if the UNDCP and the rest of the international community could help opium-producing countries like Afghanistan find alternative sources of income, "then we could very well see the possibility of a major reduction" in the drugs trade.
